title: LUPUS-BEST - Treat-to-target in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
off: LUPUS-BEST - Treat-to-target in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus. A Multicenter Two-armed Cluster-randomized Controlled Trial
summary: Multicenter, national, two-armed cluster-randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effect of a treat-to-target (T2T) strategy in in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). 14 centers will be randomized 1:1 to T2T or standard of care. Per arm 303 patients with SLE who are not in remission will be included and receive either tight control with 6-weekly visits with the aim to reach remission or SoC with control visits and treatment adjustment according to the physicians discretion. Study duration is 120 weeks using damage accrual and Health related Quality of Life as major outcomes.
desc:
This is a multicenter, national, two-armed cluster-randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effect of a treat-to-target (T2T) strategy in in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) on damage progression and health related quality of life (HRQoL). The study centers will be assigned 1:1 to standard of care (SoC) or remission, defined as the absence of clinical disease activity (clinical SLEDAI =0) AND prednisolone ≤5mg/day AND physician global assessment (PGA) \<0.5 on a VAS 0-3. Patient with SLE \> 18 years of age who are not in remission will be eligible.

Per arm, 303 patients will be included. Intervention centers receive a standardized training on T2T and shared decision making (SDM). In the intervention centers, patients not on target enter a phase of tight control with 6-weekly visits and treatment adjustments (at least 4 visits) or until remission is reached and maintained. Patients in remission are reassessed every 12 weeks. In case of flare, they can re-enter tight control based on SDM. In the SoC arm, patients receive 3- to 6-monthly controls and treatment adjustments according to the physician's discretion. Study duration is 120 weeks using damage accrual and HRQoL as major outcomes.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients with SLE according to validated classification criteria
* Age at least 18 years
* Not in a stage of remission due to

  1. Clinical SLEDAI \> 0 AND/OR
  2. GC dosage above 5 mg prednisone equivalent per day AND/OR
  3. Physician global assessment ≥ 0.5 on a visual analogue scale (VAS) from 0 to 3
* Fluent German language skills
* Written informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Participation in other interventional trial(s)
* Any disease or medical condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, would make the subject unsuitable for this study, would interfere with the interpretation of subject safety or study results, or is considered unsuitable by the investigator for any other reason. Examples could be:

  * Life-threatening SLE manifestations that require intensive care treatment
  * Active life-threatening diseases other than SLE
  * Active malignancies
  * Acute and chronic infections that do not allow the intensification of immunosuppressive treatment

arms.d: T2T will be implemented based on shared decision-making (SDM), tight control and remission as a validated treatment target (disease activity score clinical SLEDAI-2k = 0 \& glucocorticoids (GC) ≤ 5 mg prednisolone equivalent \& physician global assessment (PGA 0-3) \< 0.5 ± immunomodulatory therapy); All intervention centers will receive T2T/SDM trainings. Patients not meeting their target criterion at study entry or at any time during the trial will be included in a tight control T2T loop of 24 weeks with assessments every 6 weeks to reach the target by adjustments of their immunomodulatory treatments. Patients in target will be assessed every 12 weeks as it is standard in clinical routine care.

x.titre: LUPUS-BEST : stratégie treat-to-target dans le lupus systémique
x.question: Une stratégie treat-to-target avec contrôle rapproché réduit-elle l'accumulation de dommages dans le lupus par rapport aux soins courants ?
x.contexte:
Le lupus systémique évolue par poussées et accumule des dommages d'organe, liés à la maladie et à la corticothérapie. Les recommandations de l'EULAR et d'un consensus international (Treat-to-Target) proposent la rémission, ou à défaut une faible activité, comme cible thérapeutique avec une dose de prednisone ≤ 5 mg/jour.

La démonstration que cette stratégie réduit les dommages et améliore la qualité de vie dans un essai randomisé fait défaut. Dans la polyarthrite, le T2T a prouvé son intérêt, mais le lupus, plus hétérogène, n'a pas été testé de la même façon.

LUPUS-BEST est un essai allemand, randomisé en grappes, promu par l'université Heinrich-Heine de Düsseldorf. Quatorze centres sont randomisés 1:1 entre T2T et soins courants, avec 303 patients par bras. Dans les centres T2T, formés à la décision partagée, les patients hors cible ont des visites toutes les 6 semaines avec ajustement du traitement jusqu'à la rémission, définie par SLEDAI clinique = 0, prednisone ≤ 5 mg/jour et PGA < 0,5. Les soins courants comportent des contrôles tous les 3 à 6 mois. Le suivi est de 120 semaines.
x.interet: L'étude pourrait établir si le treat-to-target améliore les résultats à long terme dans le lupus. Un résultat positif soutiendrait l'adoption de consultations rapprochées avec cible de rémission.
x.profil: Des adultes atteints de lupus systémique non en rémission, suivis dans des centres allemands.
inclusion: Lupus selon des critères de classification validés
Absence de rémission : SLEDAI clinique > 0 et/ou prednisone > 5 mg/jour et/ou PGA ≥ 0,5
exclusion: Participation à un autre essai interventionnel
Manifestation menaçant le pronostic vital nécessitant la réanimation
Autre maladie engageant le pronostic vital, cancer actif
Infection aiguë ou chronique empêchant l'intensification de l'immunosuppression
